punchline: Chrome finished 2009 with 38 million users against a goal of 50 million, and Larry Page still called 100 million too small for the next year.
thirty_sec: Google's Chrome team set stretch targets. The 2009 goal was 50 million seven-day active users, and the year ended at 38 million. For 2010 Sundar Pichai proposed 100 million, Larry Page said that was not enough, and they settled on 111 million. Chrome reached it. Doerr writes that Google's aspirational OKRs aim at about 60 to 70 percent attainment.
